cases.failure_message: Trivy image scan found fixable vulnerabilities and make image-scan exited with Error 1.
cases.opposite_diagnosis: Trivy found four fixable vulnerabilities and the --exit-code 1 security gate fired, but temporary scanner database state caused the failure.
cases.reference_diagnosis: At the pinned commit, the driver image is compiled with Go 1.26.4 and includes google.golang.org/grpc v1.81.1 and golang.org/x/text v0.38.0. Trivy reports those exact installed versions as affected by four vulnerabilities with fixes available, and the Makefile intentionally fails the image-scan target when any fixed MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL finding is present.

cases.failure_message: error: timed out waiting for the condition on deployments/kubeflow-trainer-controller-manager; make run-test-e2e-k8s-main-was failed.
cases.opposite_diagnosis: The scheduler requested v1beta1 while the cluster served v1alpha3; PodGroup returned 404 and the handler failed to sync, but the API mismatch was incidental and a one-off image-pull delay caused the timeout.

cases.reference_diagnosis: The WAS kind configuration at the pinned Kueue revision enables GenericWorkload but explicitly serves scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha3. The job fetched Kubernetes main v1.37.0-beta.0.568+4f5591ab57b75c, whose scheduler initializes a v1beta1.PodGroup informer. The API server returned 404 for that version, so the scheduler handlers never synchronized, the Kubeflow Trainer pod remained unscheduled, and the deployment wait timed out.

cases.test_name: [It] External Storage [Driver: csi-gcepd-sc-windows--pd-volumesnapshotclass] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] provisioning should provision correct filesystem size when restoring snapshot to larger size pvc [Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource]
cases.failure_message: [FAILED] Failed to obtain filesystem size of a volume mount: resolved empty volumeID for mountPath "/mnt/volume1" at provisioning.go:525.
cases.opposite_diagnosis: The Windows mount path was absent and the volume ID was empty. NodePublishVolume did not succeed. The evidence was insufficient to distinguish ownership, but the GCE PD CSI node driver was unquestionably responsible.

forbidden.name: unsupported component ownership
forbidden.pattern: (?is)(?:(?:definitively|conclusively|unquestionably|solely|clearly).{0,180}(?:node driver|gce pd|csi.?proxy|test helper)|(?:node driver|gce pd|csi.?proxy|test helper).{0,180}(?:definitively|conclusively|unquestionably|solely|clearly|responsible|confirmed root cause))

cases.reference_diagnosis: Most likely an upstream Kubernetes Windows test/runtime mount-visibility defect at the publish-to-container handoff. The GCE PD CSI driver successfully staged and published each NTFS volume and each target pod became Running and Ready, but /mnt/volume1 was absent inside the Windows container. The failure repeated in two filesystem-size snapshot test variants on separate target pods and nodes after an earlier Windows suite passed. The available artifacts do not distinguish an incorrect or missing test volumeMount from kubelet/containerd/HCS failing to expose a valid host target, or CSI-proxy reporting symlink creation success without a usable target.
